content_metadata.description: An interview video focusing on Ron Paul's campaign and principles, especially within the GOP context.

qAndA.question: How many days are left until the South Carolina primary?

qAndA.answer: The American Research Group poll shows Ron Paul surging 11% in the past week.
qAndA.question: What evidence is there that Ron Paul's message is resonating with voters in South Carolina?

qAndA.answer: He believes restructuring is a market principle and essential for the proper functioning of the market.
qAndA.question: How does Ron Paul explain his willingness to defend Mitt Romney's business practices at Bain Capital?

qAndA.answer: He mentions Ben Bernanke's statement from 2006 claiming it was unlikely to see growth derailed by the housing market, despite the impending financial crisis.
qAndA.question: What example does Ron Paul give to illustrate his point that the Federal Reserve doesn't understand the business cycle?
What does the banner behind Ron Paul during his interview read?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: The countdown to the next GOP
primary in South Carolina is on.
We've got a new poll.
It's out from the American
research group.
It says Romney 29,
Gingrich 25,
Ron Paul 20.
By the way, that's an 11 point
surge from where Ron Paul was
just one week ago.
Congressman Paul joins us live
in just a few moments.
Welcome back to the cover report.
So after Congressman Ron Paul
strong second place finish in New Hampshire,
he is winning plot.
It's everywhere.
And I ask again this evening,
can the GOP find a home for the
principles of free market,
Austrian economic message?
Let's ask the man himself joining us now live,
Texas Republican Congressman and
presidential hopeful.
Ron Paul, Dr. Paul as always welcome back.
Before we begin sir,
take a listen to what South Carolina
Senator Jim Dement told me yesterday.
Okay.
Probably Ron Paul's the only one
willing to say we really need to cut the budget
and we need to cut some of the functions
of the federal government.
The Republicans must recognize that Ron Paul's message
of limited government, individual liberty,
more accountability at the Federal Reserve,
better monetary policy.
These are things that need to be core principles
in the Republican Party.
All right.
Congressman Paul, you heard the influential
Senator Jim Dement,
influential in South Carolina and across the country.
Do you believe now?
Okay.
After your semi victory in New Hampshire,
you had a good close second.
Do you believe that there's room
and the GOP for your principles?
Well, there better be or there won't be much left
to the party because we're really talking about
the fundamentals that they claim they believed in
for a long time.
I mean, for cutting spending and bouncing budgets
and sound money.
I mean, that's what we've talked about,
you know, all the way back to the 80s,
but we never followed through is a problem.
And then in this century, you know,
in the first decade,
we had the House of the Senate and the presidency.
And I think we blew it.
We doubled the size of the Department of Education.
We had prescription drug program.
And then we had that Sarabane's auction.
I'm told that could have cost the business community
a trillion dollars.
So, no, I think they better pay attention
to those of us who believe in free markets
and not just give lip service to us
or, you know, they're not going to do well.
Congressman Charles Krauthammer of all people
wrote a very complimentary article about you.
And I want to ask you about one of his key points.
He believes that if you can't get the nomination,
you should deliver one of the key note speeches
at the Republican Convention to push your principles.
Would you do that?
Would you give a key note speech?
Is that something that appeals to you?
Well, I think so.
I don't want them to write it for me,
but I appreciate Charles's comments.
He's another fellow physician, I guess you know.
So, I think that's a real nice compliment,
but of course, if I could write the speech,
I think I'd be very interested in doing it.
All right, good.
Now, on to South Carolina.
As you know, it's a pro defense state.
There's a lot of military bases, there's contractors,
there's builders.
You have a relatively anti-war message.
Are there going to be difficulties on that point?
You're closing pretty good,
but is the defense message going to be difficult
for South Carolina primary voters?
Well, so far, I don't think so,
because we have ads running down there,
and I think that's helped switch some people over.
And I think most people are aware of the fact
that I get twice as much money
from active military personnel
than all the other Republican candidates put together.
So, I'm getting a lot of support from the military,
and I always got a lot of support from veterans.
So, I think it's a fallacy to think
that everybody in the military,
automatically wants to expand war.
I remember the 60s, I was in,
that's the last thing I wanted to be jailed to do in 1965,
was to expand the war and be at NOM
and go over in the Cambodia,
that concerned me to a great deal.
So, I think that's a normal reaction,
but I think people going in the military
to defend the country, and they're willing to do it.
But if it's fighting a war that isn't declared
or under a UN banner or NATO,
and you get bogged down for 10 years,
and it contributes to our financial crisis,
people can get pretty tired of that.
And I think the American people are real tired
of our foreign policy in the Middle East right now.
You have copiously avoided attacking Mitt Romney,
and the Bain Capital flag about private equity companies.
Obviously, Gingrich and Perry have.
Why have you avoided attacking Mitt Romney?
What point, what principle do you want to make on this?
Well, of course, I'm willing to attack him on,
on some of the policies that he's had before,
and we disagree on, I've done that,
and use the word flip-flopping on many occasions.
But not attacking on bains,
they've asked me about it,
and I said explicitly that that's part of the market.
That's the way the market works.
Restructuring is a market principle.
And those who are jumping on him,
either they don't understand economics,
or if they do understand economics,
they're demagoguing the issue for trying to make a political point.
So in that sense, you know, it came,
it looked like I was defending Mitt,
and in that case, I was,
because it's very important that you cleanse a system.
If a company's going bankrupt,
and you don't have restructuring, everybody suffers.
And if you can get some restructuring,
and you can create jobs,
I don't know the details of everything he did,
and I don't want to vouch for that.
But the whole principle that they were attacking him on,
I think it was false.
Besides, they misquoted him anyway.
All he said was, you know, that,
well, if a company doesn't provide his service for me,
I should change companies.
Well, if you don't understand, that's important.
That's what a businessman would do.
Let me ask you, Fed question, I can't resist.
The minutes of the Fed's meeting five years ago,
and they unlocked these minutes
with a five-year time lag.
It shows in the transcript, sir,
that Bernanke and company completely missed
the financial and housing meltdown.
In fact, in 2006, where these minutes come from,
Bernanke said, it is unlikely to see growth derailed
by the housing market.
Now, the Federal Reserve System has hundreds of PhD economists.
How is it possible that they completely missed
the worst meltdown since the 1930s?
Because they follow the wrong ideas on economics,
and they don't look at the business cycle
being related to what they're doing at the Fed.
Otherwise, they would have to indict themselves.
So, and he was falling through with Greenspan.
He was doing the same thing, and they were in total denial.
But you know that if you go back and look
at some of the Austrian economists and the Hayekians
and Misiens, they explain this.
They were right about it.
The only thing that we don't claim is that we know
the exact day the bubble will burst.
But we can identify bubbles.
We know where they come from.
And when they burst, you have to have a correction.
And then you have to have unemployment.
But the more you interfere with the correction,
the longer the correction lasts.
And this is why this correction is lingering
and why if we don't get more people
to understand the business cycle,
the fact that I think you make an important point,
they have hundreds of economists
all through the university system.
But they know they don't get the job unless they say
what the Fed wants them to say.
There's no independence.
I don't ever expect independent thinking
at the Federal Reserve.
They're there to defend a policy is a total failure
and has been and we have to change it.
All right, we have to change it.
Many thanks, Congressman Ron Paulister.
Good luck on the campaign trail.
We appreciate you coming back.
